What it showed (exactly two lines of output):
1. `src/pt_bvh.cpp:399:    std::vector<unsigned int> block(bvh.nodes.size(), kInvalidNode);` — the single occurrence, and it was the line I had just written inside the new quantize_bvh (the per-node block-index array, initialized to "no block", since leaves carry no child-pair block).
2. From the companion grep for constants in the same file: `21:constexpr float kInfinity = 1e30f;` — i.e. the file's only file-scope constant.

So the grep confirmed the symbol was used but never declared anywhere (no hits in include/*.hpp, no definition in pt_bvh.cpp). I then added `kInvalidNode` next to `kInfinity` and continued with the API switch to PtBvhChild.

Yes. While rewriting quantize_bvh for the child-pair layout I suspected the new code referenced a constant that did not exist yet, so I ran: grep -rn 'kInvalidNode' src/pt_bvh.cpp include/*.hpp (plus a companion grep -n 'constexpr|static const' src/pt_bvh.cpp).

It showed exactly one match — src/pt_bvh.cpp:399: `std::vector<unsigned int> block(bvh.nodes.size(), kInvalidNode);` — which was my own just-written line inside quantize_bvh. Nothing in include/*.hpp or anywhere else defined it, and the constexpr grep listed only `constexpr float kInfinity = 1e30f;` at src/pt_bvh.cpp:21. In other words the grep proved kInvalidNode was an undefined symbol, so the build would have failed.

I fixed it by adding `constexpr unsigned int kInvalidNode = 0xFFFFFFFFu;` immediately after kInfinity in pt_bvh.cpp (the value means "no block", matching the per-node block index table used to assign pre-order child-block indices).

How I know: this is recorded verbatim in my history — the grep result is message #140 and the edit that added the constant is message #141; both are in my archived round-5 segment and I re-read them just now rather than paraphrasing from memory.
